    LATAM Therapists & Clinicians — Parental Alienation Practitioner Directory¶

    Schema version: 1.0 Last updated: 2026-05-25 License: CC BY 4.0 (intended for github.com/AntiAlienate/antialienate-knowledge) Region: LATAM (BR / MX / AR / CO / CL) Scope: Latin-American psychiatrists, psychologists (clinical / forensic / academic), psicólogos peritos, and clinical social workers who have (a) worked PA cases as treating clinician or court-appointed expert (perito forense / perito judicial), (b) published on alienação parental / alienación parental in a peer-reviewed venue or recognised professional publication, or © publicly stated a sourced stance (recognition / critique / middle) on PA. Institutional entries (national psychology councils, national child-protection bodies, victim-services networks) are listed where the institution itself has issued a sourced PA position.

    Standards: Primary sources only — national register entries where searchable, practice / institutional website, peer-reviewed publications, court records, named press. Where a fact could not be confirmed from a public primary source it is flagged "not publicly confirmed".

    Stance taxonomy: - recognition — treats alienação parental / alienación parental as a real, assessable phenomenon; operates or endorses PA-specific assessment, expert-witness or reunification work; typically PASG / CEAP / GARI-PA-aligned. - critique — argues the PA construct (especially Gardner's SAP) is operationalised against DV / coercive-control survivors (predominantly mothers and children); advocates DV/trauma-informed alternatives and tighter regulation of expert witnesses; supports repeal of Lei 12.318/2010 or jurisprudential proscription as in Colombia 2023. - middle — engages both alienating-behaviour and family-violence frames; differential-diagnosis or systemic / multi-family approach; not aligned with PASG and not in the abolitionist critique camp.

    Critical LATAM regulatory & policy context (must read before using this directory):

    • Brazil (BR): Psychologists are registered with one of 24 Conselhos Regionais de Psicologia (CRP) (e.g. CRP-RJ 05, CRP-SP 06) under the Conselho Federal de Psicologia (CFP), https://site.cfp.org.br/. The 2022 CFP Nota Técnica nº 4/2022/GTEC/CG (https://site.cfp.org.br/wp-content/uploads/2022/08/SEI_CFP-0698871-Nota-Tecnica.pdf) is the institutional doctrinal anchor: it instructs psicólogos not to ground analyses on Lei 12.318/2010 as a clinical construct, and recognises PA allegations as predominantly affecting guardian mothers with a gender bias. IBDFAM and a substantial recognition-camp clinical literature (Calçada, Brazil, Perissini) push back. Lei 12.318/2010 + Lei 14.340/2022 remain in force; CCJ approved PL 1.372/2023 (full revocation) 37-28 on 3 Dec 2025.
    • Mexico (MX): Psicólogos hold a cédula profesional issued by the Dirección General de Profesiones / SEP (https://www.cedulaprofesional.sep.gob.mx/); there is no single binding national colegio of psychologists. State civil codes diverge on alienación parental — CDMX (Civil Code reform 2022), Estado de México and others incorporate it; SCJN Acción de Inconstitucionalidad 11/2016 (Oaxaca) struck down the criminal/loss-of-custody automaticity. The 2021 SCJN Protocolo para Juzgar con Perspectiva de Infancia y Adolescencia (https://www.scjn.gob.mx/derechos-humanos/sites/default/files/protocolos/archivos/2021-11/Protocolo%20para%20juzgar%20con%20perspectiva%20de%20IA%2010nov21.pdf) is the doctrinal anchor.
    • Argentina (AR): Psicólogos register with provincial colegios (e.g. Colegio de Psicólogos de la Provincia de Buenos Aires https://www.colpsiba.org.ar/, CPCBA for CABA https://www.psicologos.org.ar/); psiquiatras with the APSA / Asociación Argentina de Psiquiatras and provincial colegios médicos. Ley 24.270 criminalises obstruction of contact (1993) but does not codify SAP. ASAPMI (https://asapmi.org.ar/) is the leading professional society publishing the critique-camp position; CEAP Argentina (https://alienacionparental.com.ar/) is the recognition-camp institutional pole.
    • Colombia (CO): Psicólogos register with COLPSIC – Colegio Colombiano de Psicólogos (https://www.colpsic.org.co/) and obtain the tarjeta profesional. The institutional doctrine pivoted in November 2023: COLPSIC issued Posición Gremial sobre Alienación Parental (16 Nov 2023 — https://www.colpsic.org.co/comunicados/posicion-del-colegio-colombiano-de-psicologos-colpsic-frente-al-concepto-de-alienacion-parental/), and on 30 Nov 2023 the Corte Constitucional Sentencia T-526/23 (https://www.corteconstitucional.gov.co/relatoria/2023/t-526-23.htm) proscribed SAP as a criterion for judicial analysis of children's testimony. The ICBF – Instituto Colombiano de Bienestar Familiar (https://www.icbf.gov.co/) is the institutional family-court psychology body referenced in T-526.
    • Chile (CL): Psicólogos register with the Colegio de Psicólogos de Chile (https://www.colegiopsicologos.cl/) — collegiate membership is voluntary post-1981. SENAME / mejor niñez (https://www.mejorninez.cl/) is the national child-protection service. There is no entity in Chile that institutionally addresses alienación parental and it is neither a crime nor a clinical diagnosis in the Chilean health system; the principal clinical voices are individual academics (Pinto-Cortez at UTA; Portilla-Saavedra and Moya-Vergara at UCN) and the Instituto Chileno de Terapia Familiar (IChTF) for the middle / family-systems camp.

    Cross-references to other antialienate-knowledge directories: - Mauricio Luis Mizrahi (Argentina) is in /practitioners-latam-lawyers.md as a jurist; he chairs CEAP Argentina but is not a therapist — kept in the lawyers file. Pedro Herscovici (psychiatrist) is the CEAP psychiatric pairing and is the AR recognition-camp clinical entry here. - William Bernet (USA, CEAP member, GARI-PA), Asunción Tejedor Huerta (ES) — full entries in /practitioners-us-therapists.md and /practitioners-eu-therapists.md respectively. - Sonia Vaccaro (Argentine-born, Madrid-based clinical/forensic psychologist) is principally listed in /practitioners-eu-therapists.md under Spain; cross-listed at end of Argentina section here because she is the most cited Spanish-language critique-camp clinician on the Argentine PA debate. - CFP Brazil Nota Técnica 4/2022 is also cited in /jurisdictions/brazil/ and in /evidence-international-institutional-positions.md. - COLPSIC 2023 position + Corte Constitucional T-526/23 are in /case-studies/ and in /evidence-international-institutional-positions.md.

    Brazil¶

    Brazil's clinical-psychology terrain is uniquely polarised in 2026. The CFP Nota Técnica 4/2022 institutionally instructs psicólogos not to ground their analyses in Lei 12.318/2010; IBDFAM and a strong São Paulo / Rio recognition-camp clinical literature (Calçada, Brazil, Perissini) push back. Practitioners cluster sharply by camp.

    • Regulatory body: CRP-05 (Rio de Janeiro) — Psicóloga, with declared CRP 05/18785 (per A Psicodinâmica da Alienação Parental author byline mirrored at https://escuelamunduna.edu.ar/sites/default/files/A%20Psicodin%C3%A2mica%20da%20Aliena%C3%A7%C3%A3o%20Parental%20%20Andreia%20Cal%C3%A7ada_0.pdf)
    • Registration number: CRP 05/18785 (as displayed on her published work)
    • Specialty: Psicologia clínica e jurídica; perícia psicológica forense em Varas de Família; alienação parental; falsas alegações de abuso sexual em disputas de guarda; psicodiagnóstico; neuropsicologia

Perdas Irreparáveis: Alienação Parental e Falsas Acusações de Abuso Sexual (Equilíbrio) — 20+ years of expert-witness practice synthesised; A Psicodinâmica da Alienação Parental (PDF above); Calçada et al., Perícia psicológica forense em processos que envolvem acusações de alienação parental (Revista Científica do IBDFAM, ed. 45) — IBDFAM coverage https://ibdfam.org.br/noticias/9049/Per%C3%ADcia+psicol%C3%B3gica+forense+em+processos+de+aliena%C3%A7%C3%A3o+parental+%C3%A9+enfoque+de+artigo+na+Revista+Cient%C3%ADfica+do+IBDFAM ; member of the Comissão Científica of Revista Alienação Parental https://revistaalienacaoparental.webnode.pt/comissao-cientifica/
    • Programs / publications:

    • Co-author of the IBDFAM Revista Científica article on perícia psicológica forense em processos de alienação parental (ed. 45)
    • Recurring Migalhas columnist (https://www.migalhas.com.br/autor/andreia-soares-calcada)

    • Tier: 1

    • Notes: Team CRP numbers (collaborating psicólogas Coutinho Kuczny CRP 08/33462, Amin CRP 05/68002, Cardoso CRP 05/54838) are publicly displayed on her practice site — useful as registry verification.

    • Registration number: not publicly displayed on personal site

    • Stance: recognition
    • Stance source: Brazil, A Alienação Parental sob a Ótica da Neurociência (IBDFAM PDF) https://ibdfam.org.br/assets/img/upload/files/Artigo%20IBDFAM%20glicia.pdf ; Intercept profile "Glicia Brazil: a psicóloga que ajuda na defesa de acusados de abuso" https://www.intercept.com.br/2023/05/18/abuso-glicia-brazil-psicologa-fortalece-defesa-de-acusados/ ; GEN webinar Alienação Parental: Detecção, Aspectos Legais e Processuais https://blog.grupogen.com.br/juridico/areas-de-interesse/civil/live-alienacao-parental/ ; IBDFAM coverage of Mês de Combate à Alienação Parental https://ibdfam.org.br/noticias/10711

    • Notes: Intercept (May 2023) ran a critical investigation framing her as "the psychologist who helps the defence of accused [abusers]" — high media-sensitivity entry. Use as a flashpoint figure; she is currently the principal target of feminist coalition critique in the BR PA clinical debate.

    • Tier: 2
    • Hook: The Brazilian critique-camp clinical-academic author whose 2010 Cortez monograph remains the most circulated Portuguese-language critical book on Lei 12.318/2010.

    Mexico¶

    Mexico's PA-clinical landscape is sparse but polarised: SCJN's 2021 Protocolo para Juzgar con Perspectiva de Infancia y Adolescencia and Acción de Inconstitucionalidad 11/2016 (Oaxaca) frame the doctrinal critique anchor; the recognition camp is concentrated in GARI-PA / PASG-Hispanic under Mendoza-Amaro. There is no Mexican equivalent of CFP NT 4/2022.

    Argentina¶

    Argentina's PA-clinical terrain is the most institutionally polarised in LATAM: ASAPMI (critique) vs CEAP Argentina (recognition), with Eva Giberti as the single most senior pioneer-clinician on the critique pole.

    Colombia¶

    Colombia's PA-clinical terrain pivoted decisively to the critique pole in November 2023: COLPSIC issued its Posición Gremial (16 Nov) and the Corte Constitucional Sentencia T-526/23 (30 Nov) proscribed SAP as a judicial criterion. The clinical recognition-camp infrastructure is thin compared to Brazil / Argentina.

    • Country / city: CO / Bogotá (national sede; 7 capítulos regionales)

    2. INSTITUTIONAL — Instituto Colombiano de Bienestar Familiar (ICBF)¶

    • Country / city: CO / Bogotá (national; territorial direcciones in all 32 departments)
    • Institution: ICBF — national family-welfare institute (creado 1968); under Departamento Administrativo para la Prosperidad Social; institucional family-court psychology and defensorías de familia network
    • Institutional URLs: https://www.icbf.gov.co/ ; El Instituto https://www.icbf.gov.co/instituto ; Puntos de Atención https://www.icbf.gov.co/instituto/puntos-atencion ; Directorio Servidores Públicos https://www.icbf.gov.co/sites/default/files/files/Directorio%20Servidores%20P%C3%BAblicos.pdf
    • Regulatory body: Federal (Departamento Administrativo para la Prosperidad Social)
    • Specialty: Defensorías de familia; psicología familiar institucional; intervención en procesos de restablecimiento de derechos de niños, niñas y adolescentes; intervención técnica en procesos de custodia ante jueces de familia
    • Stance: critique-adjacent (institutional — ICBF intervention in T-526/23 stated COLPSIC does not support SAP as a diagnostic category)
    • Stance source: ICBF's institutional intervention is cited in Corte Constitucional Sentencia T-526/23 (30 Nov 2023) as the channel through which the Court learned of COLPSIC's non-support of SAP — see desclab analysis 4 claves para entender la Sentencia T-526 de 2023 https://www.desclab.com/post/alienacion ; ICBF Lineamientos Técnicos para la Atención Integral a Niños, Niñas y Adolescentes operate as the doctrinal anchor for defensorías de familia psychology
    • Programs / publications:
    • Intervention in Corte Constitucional T-526/23 (citing COLPSIC non-support of SAP)
    • Lineamientos Técnicos para Atención Integral (institutional methodology)
    • Directorio de servidores públicos (psicólogos institucionales) https://www.icbf.gov.co/sites/default/files/files/Directorio%20Servidores%20P%C3%BAblicos.pdf
    • Primary contact: AtencionAlCiudadano@icbf.gov.co ; Sede Nacional, Av. Cra 68 No 64C-75, Bogotá D.C. — https://www.icbf.gov.co/
    • Tier: 2
    • Hook: The Colombian national family-welfare institution whose psychology corps operationalises T-526/23 on the ground; the institutional contact for defensorías de familia methodology questions.

    Colombia — entries considered and excluded¶

    • Pilar Asunción Aguirre — no primary source retrievable confirming a Colombian psicóloga by that name working on PA. Not publicly confirmed — excluded.
    • Andrés Tello Cabello — the retrievable "Andrés Tello" hits are a Chilean sociologist (Data Justa) and a Colombian food-industry executive; no Colombian psicólogo by that name with confirmable PA work. Not publicly confirmed — excluded.
    • Individual recognition-camp Colombian psicólogos — the practice site Legalan Abogados (Medellín) and prior 2017 COLPSIC Unidad de Psicología Jurídica y Forense report exist as evidence of a prior pro-recognition camp, but post-T-526/23 the institutional space has collapsed and no individual recognition-camp Colombian psicólogo with confirmable practice site + sourced stance + named publication is publicly retrievable as of 2026-05-25. Honest finding: Colombia's recognition-camp clinical infrastructure is institutionally orphaned after T-526.

    Chile¶

    Chile has no institutional doctrinal anchor on PA — alienación parental is neither a crime nor a Chilean clinical diagnosis (per SENAME / mejor niñez). The principal clinical voices are individual academics at UCN / UTA / IChTF. The recognition camp is concentrated in Pinto-Cortez (UTA) + Portilla-Saavedra & Moya-Vergara (UCN) via a single 2023 peer-reviewed paper; the middle-camp anchor is Claudia Cáceres (IChTF).

    1. Dr Cristián Pinto-Cortez, PhD¶

    • Country / city: CL / Arica (Región de Arica y Parinacota)
    • Practice / affiliation: Professor / investigator, Escuela de Psicología y Filosofía, Facultad de Ciencias Sociales y Jurídicas, Universidad de Tarapacá (UTA), Arica
    • Practice URLs: UTA Escuela de Psicología (institutional) ; published paper https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10528598/
    • Regulatory body: Psicólogo — Universidad de Tarapacá institutional credentialing; Colegio de Psicólogos de Chile membership not publicly displayed (colegiación voluntaria post-1981)
    • Registration number: not publicly displayed
    • Specialty: Psicología clínica e infantil; victimización infantil; parental alienating behaviors as a specific form of psychological/emotional child maltreatment; psychometric assessment of PAB exposure
    • Stance: recognition (academic — frames PAB as child maltreatment producing measurable adult mental health sequelae)
    • Stance source: Portilla-Saavedra, Pinto-Cortez & Moya-Vergara (2023) Psychological Distress in Young Chilean Adults Exposed to Parental Alienating Behaviors during Childhood/Adolescence, European Journal of Investigation in Health, Psychology and Education — PMC https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10528598/ ; cited as canonical Chilean empirical paper on PAB → mental-health outcomes
    • Programs / publications:
    • Portilla-Saavedra, Pinto-Cortez & Moya-Vergara (2023) — the canonical Chilean peer-reviewed empirical paper on PAB
    • UTA Escuela de Psicología y Filosofía research program on victimización infantil
    • Primary contact: cpinto@academicos.uta.cl ; UTA Arica institutional channel
    • Tier: 2
    • Hook: The single most-cited Chilean academic on PAB → adult mental-health outcomes. The natural Chilean academic contact for the recognition-camp empirical-evidence frame.

    Chile — entries considered and excluded¶

    • Soledad Espinoza — no primary source retrievable confirming a Chilean clinical psychologist by that name working on PA. Not publicly confirmed — excluded.
    • Vania Apablaza — no primary source retrievable. Not publicly confirmed — excluded.
    • Corporación Humanas — Santiago feminist legal NGO; no PA-specific institutional position publicly retrievable as of 2026-05-25; excluded for lack of sourced PA stance.
    • Programa SENAME / Servicio Nacional de Menores (now mejor niñez) — national child-protection service. There is no SENAME / mejor niñez institutional position on alienación parental publicly retrievable; SENAME does not address PA as a clinical category (per CIPER Chile 2013 Crisis del SENAME https://www.ciperchile.cl/2013/08/19/crisis-del-sename-un-sistema-que-hiere-cuando-intenta-cuidar/ and SENAME Enfoque document https://www.sename.cl/wsename/otros/2012/enfoque.pdf). Excluded for lack of PA-specific institutional doctrine. Honest finding: Chile is the LATAM jurisdiction with the least institutional clinical engagement on PA either way.

    Honest gaps¶

    • Mexico critique-camp clinician individual entry: None publicly confirmable. CONAVIM, INMUJERES and CEAV have not issued sourced PA-specific clinical positions; the critique side is represented institutionally only via the SCJN Protocolo (middle / procedural). This is a real LATAM gap — Mexico has a vigorous feminist legal critique of PA-statute use but a thin individual clinician-author footprint.
    • Colombia individual recognition-camp clinician: Institutionally orphaned post-T-526/23. The pre-2023 pro-recognition position of COLPSIC's Unidad de Psicología Jurídica y Forense (2017) was institutionally retracted Nov 2023; no individual Colombian psicólogo with a current public-facing PA-recognition practice site + sourced stance is retrievable.
    • Chile institutional doctrine on PA: Does not exist. SENAME / mejor niñez does not address PA; Colegio de Psicólogos has issued no equivalent of COLPSIC's Posición Gremial. Chile is the LATAM jurisdiction with the least institutional clinical engagement on PA in either direction.
    • CRP / colegio numbers: Only Calçada (CRP 05/18785) and her collaborating team have publicly displayed Brazilian CRP numbers. Argentine psiquiatra colegio numbers and Mexican cédulas profesionales are generally not publicly displayed on practitioner sites; verification requires direct lookup via the relevant national register before formal outreach.
    • Specific PA-publication confirmation for senior names: Eva Giberti's PA-specific publications are dispersed across Página/12 columns and book chapters rather than peer-reviewed clinical literature; her stance is sourced via institutional role (Programa Las Víctimas) and named-press alignment, not a single peer-reviewed PA paper.
